title: Neutral wire report
text:
HARBOURTON, Nov 12 – The Harbourton city council on Tuesday approved a plan to replace about 40,000 electricity meters by the end of 2027, the council said in a statement.

The project will cost an estimated 18 million euros, according to the council's budget document, and will be partly funded by a national energy-efficiency grant.

Council member Liis Tamm, who voted against the plan, said the timeline was “too tight for a project of this size”. Utility spokesperson Mark Ellis said households would be notified at least two weeks before installation.

The new meters report consumption every 15 minutes. Residents who prefer not to receive one can apply for an exemption, the utility said.

title: Opinion column
text:
I have lived in Harbourton for twenty years, and I think the smart-meter plan deserves a harder look than it got. The council promises lower bills, but it has not published the figures behind that promise.

To be fair, the old meters are unreliable, and supporters of the plan have a point when they say manual readings waste money. Still, a project costing 18 million euros should come with a public cost-benefit analysis, not just a press release.

We should ask for that analysis before installation starts. If the numbers hold up, I will be glad to be proven wrong.
